title: Usability is not aesthetic taste

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Yesterday we asked whether Maya's whole attempt worked. Today the team wants me to choose between two booking screens. One is beautiful.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: And the other?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Also beautiful. That's the problem. What am I comparing?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Try rescheduling Maya's appointment on each one. Tell me what happens.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: On the first, I can check a new time before I give up the old one. On the second… wait, tapping the new slot cancels the original.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Would Maya know that before she tapped?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: No. Both screens look calm. Only one lets her act safely.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: That's our chapter: usability. We'll look at whether someone can reach the right result, how much work it takes, whether they understand it, and how they recover when things go wrong.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: So not, ‘Which one do you like?’

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Not as your first test. Set the task and context. Who is using it? What are they trying to do? What would count as a serious mistake?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Maya is changing an appointment on her phone between meetings. The right result is a slot she can attend, without losing the old one by accident.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Now watch, without helping her. Did she choose the right clinic and time? That's effectiveness.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: How long she spent, what she reread, and whether she had to call for help: efficiency.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: And if she chose wrongly?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Recovery. She needs a safe way back. I can't call a flow usable just because it was fast on the happy path.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Exactly. Ask what she believes happened, too.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: She submitted the change. The screen says ‘Request received.’ If she thinks that means confirmed, our completion metric flatters us.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: What would you change?

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: Show requested, under review, confirmed, or action required as different states. Name who acts next. Keep the information she's entered and let her change course.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Good. A plain screen that gets that right may be more usable than a polished one that hides the risk.

turns.speaker: alex
turns.text: And next lesson we ask how that working journey should leave her feeling.
